sentences.sentence: The NHS lists trapped wind, indigestion, constipation and a stomach bug or food poisoning as common everyday causes of stomach ache.

sentences.sentence: Period pain and endometriosis are listed as causes of pain in the lower tummy in women.
sentences.note: Summary 'lower abdomen (women)' from nhs.uk stomach ache; page attribution not exact.

sentences.sentence: The NHS stomach ache page links pain in the lower right side of the tummy with appendicitis.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: It links severe pain that lasts up to 8 hours in the centre of the tummy, or just under the ribs on the right, with gallstones.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: It links ongoing cramps, bloating, diarrhoea and constipation with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform describes appendicitis as painful swelling of the appendix, and says the pain of IBS is often relieved by going to the toilet.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Stomach ulcer pain is usually in the upper tummy, may feel burning and is often worse at night.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Gastritis can cause pain, indigestion and feeling sick.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Gastritis is inflammation of the lining of the stomach.
sentences.note: Plain textbook definition.

sentences.sentence: Acute pancreatitis causes severe pain that develops suddenly in the centre of the tummy, and the NHS says its most common causes are gallstones and drinking a lot of alcohol.
sentences.note: Summary: severe pain developing suddenly in the centre; common causes gallstones or alcohol (acute pancreatitis pages).

sentences.sentence: Appendicitis is when the appendix becomes inflamed; it usually causes pain in the lower right side of the tummy and is sometimes accompanied by nausea and loss of appetite.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: An NHS 111 Wales page says appendicitis needs urgent treatment in hospital.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A hospital trust page says gallstones do not always cause symptoms, but can lead to pain after eating, inflammation of the gallbladder, pancreatitis or jaundice.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says diverticular disease causes pain in the lower left side of the tummy that often gets worse after eating and eases after passing wind or stool, with constipation, diarrhoea, bloating or blood in the stool.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: It adds that the symptoms are similar to those of other conditions such as IBS.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: For diverticular disease the NHS advises an urgent GP appointment or NHS 111 for blood in the stool, worsening or persistent tummy pain, or a fever, and says to call 999 or go to A&E for severe tummy pain with vomiting, a swollen tummy, being unable to pass stool or wind, or signs of sepsis.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to call 999 or go to A&E if the pain started suddenly and is severe.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Other reasons are vomiting blood or vomit that looks green or like ground coffee, a lot of blood from the bottom or black, sticky poo, being unable to pee at all, being unable to poo or fart at all, a rash that does not fade when pressed, or struggling to breathe.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform adds chest pain, and pain that hurts when the stomach is touched, to the reasons to call 999.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: For acute pancreatitis, the NHS says to call 999 or go to A&E if the pain spreads to the back, or if there is a fast heartbeat or difficulty breathing.
sentences.note: Summary attributed this to acute pancreatitis pages.

sentences.sentence: The NHS advises an urgent GP appointment or NHS 111 if the ache suddenly gets much worse, if the person is pregnant, if there is blood in the poo, or if diarrhoea or vomiting has lasted several days.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: It advises a GP appointment for pain, bloating or indigestion that does not go away or keeps coming back, for a lump in the tummy, or for losing weight without trying.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Treatment depends on the cause.
sentences.note: Summary: treatment depends on the cause (general across pages).

sentences.sentence: For gastritis, a GP might arrange a breath test for Helicobacter pylori bacteria, a stool test or a blood test.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Stomach ulcers may be treated with antibiotics for a Helicobacter pylori infection or with medicines that reduce stomach acid, such as proton pump inhibitors.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Gastroenteritis often has no specific treatment, and the illness has to run its course.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).
